GATOH Quickstart

The Generalised Agent Transformation of Opinions in Hierarchies, or GATOH, framework is an agent-based modeling library for Python. It is designed to provide a highly flexible and generalisable framework that can define and simulate a wide variety of agent-based models centered on opinion dynamics.

Installing GATOH

GATOH has been primarily developed and tested on a x86_64 Linux system, but support for 64 bit Windows has also been confirmed. The different methods for installing GATOH are outlined below:

  1. Ensure that Python >=3.14 is installed on your system.

  2. Clone the library’s code from the git repository: git clone https://github.com/JungleHollow/GATOH.

  3. If needed, create a virtual environment to install the library to.

  4. From the target python environment, simply install GATOH using pip as normal, but specify the path to the GATOH directory rather than the package name: python -m pip install <path to GATOH directory>.

  5. At this point, all required dependencies will be installed alongside GATOH, and you can begin using the library.

Using GATOH

Once you have installed GATOH, you can use it by importing gatoh in your python scripts. Almost all functions and classes in GATOH are currently organised into their own submodules, meaning that these will need to be imported and used accordingly. Below is a simple example of what very basic GATOH usage could look like:

from gatoh.model import ABModel
from gatoh.utils import plot_graph

HIERARCHIES = ["Religious", "Neighbours", "Family", "Friends"]
HIERARCHY_RW = {
    "Religious": (0.0, 0.3),
    "Neighbours": (0.0, 0.2),
    "Family": (0.0, 0.01),
    "Friends": (0.0, 0.1),
}

model = ABModel(
    HIERARCHIES,
    HIERARCHY_RW,
    iterations=50,
    model_id="TEST_MODEL",
)
model.generate_agents(
    "TEST",
    {
        "neutral": 0.4,
        "social": 0.4,
        "impulsive": 0.2,
    },
    number=20,
)
model.generate_graphs(
    HIERARCHIES,
    model.agents,
    method="blockmodel",
    agent_subsetting=True,
)

model.iterate()

x_vals = {"iterations": [i for i in range(50)]}
y_vals = {"aggregate_opinions": model.logger.variables.aggregate_opinions}

plot_graph(
    x_vals,
    y_vals,
    ...
)

You can refer to the Basic tutorial for more information on how to use GATOH, or the Absolute beginner’s guide for an in-depth explanation of agent-based modeling and the GATOH framework.
